_comment: Conditions (afflictions and lingering effects). 'effect': damage = lose 'dice' HP per tick · skip = lose the turn · stat = while it lasts, the listed modifiers apply (hit / dmg / ac / saves — negative numbers weaken; the combat log names the condition beside the number) · slow = acts on even rounds only, like a speed-2 monster. 'breaks_on_damage': true (Sleep) = any damage shakes it off. In battle a condition ticks at the START of the afflicted creature's own initiative turn. 'lingers': false = it expires when the battle ends; true = it follows you onto the map, ticking every 'map_tick_every' map turns (camp is 50 turns — sleep off a poison at your peril). 'save': which ability resists when something tries to inflict it (monsters use their save bonus). 'color' paints the floating text and status pips. Magic v3 (2026-08-28) added sleep/slowed/weakened/frightened/blinded — monsters' 'inflicts' and gear 'immune' lists may use them too. Edit freely and refresh! | 'icon' (2026-09-02): the emoji badge drawn on battle tiles and sidebar cards — swap any glyph freely; no icon falls back to a colored pip. | 'fear': true (2026-09-02) = behavioral fear: the afflicted cannot move toward whoever caused it (the engine remembers the source).

burning.name: Burning
burning.description: Fire clings — damage each round until it gutters out

poison.name: Poisoned
poison.description: Venom in the blood — ticks in battle and on the march

exhaustion.name: Exhausted
exhaustion.description: Utterly spent — the next turn is lost (channeling backlash and the like)

paralysis.name: Paralyzed
paralysis.description: Frozen stiff — the turn is lost

sleep.name: Asleep
sleep.description: Slumped and dreaming — the turn is lost, until something hurts

slowed.name: Slowed
slowed.description: Mired — acts only every other round

weakened.name: Weakened
weakened.description: Strength runs out like water — −2 to hit and damage

frightened.name: Frightened
frightened.description: Cowed — −2 to hit, −2 on every save, and no step may close the distance to the source of the terror
